turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, and I'd like to start with why my son found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class before anyone called me. Who decided that, and when?
I spoke with the vice principal before you came in.

Before I came in. The zero went into the gradebook on November 3, so today's conversation with the vice principal doesn't answer my question. Did anyone speak to Owen before that mark was entered, yes or no?
She's backing me completely. Policy is policy, and it isn't up to you.

"Policy is policy." Then you'll know 4.2 says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me, so show me the vice principal's backing in writing, because right now it's your word. And no, it isn't up to me, Hale, it's up to the principal, and that's where I'm going if you can't answer whether Owen was heard first.
So frankly, this meeting is a courtesy.
"A courtesy." I'm writing that down, Hale, next to the date the zero went in and the fact that nobody called me first. Now, what do you actually have on Owen's essay, or am I going upstairs?
